timeline.title: Logging Admission by Amy Keogh
timeline.event: Brighton Fringe confirmed it had been logging all police reports and emails from Ben, without disclosing this previously.

timeline.title: Unlawful Disclosure to NHS
timeline.event: Brighton Fringe emailed the complainant's GP without consent, citing mental health instability and internal justifications for removal.

timeline.title: Mass Libel Email to Artists and Clients
timeline.event: Brighton Fringe emailed 160+ stakeholders to remove Ben Carter without acknowledging prior safeguarding disclosures or allowing rebuttal.

timeline.title: SAR Initiated to Seven Dials Medical Centre
timeline.event: Ben Carter submits a formal Subject Access Request to Seven Dials GP surgery regarding medical record manipulation and third-party disclosures.

timeline.title: SAR Scope Clarified
timeline.event: Ben clarifies that he is requesting all communication logs, edit histories, and third-party contact records. Legal SAR clock begins.

timeline.title: SAR Deadline Breached – No Response
timeline.event: No disclosure or lawful extension notice is received. Seven Dials is now in breach of GDPR Art. 12(3) and 15.

timeline.title: Final Warning + Litigation Hold Issued
timeline.event: Ben issues a preservation notice and 7-day final deadline, referencing Brighton Fringe and coercion pattern.

timeline.event: Screenshot from the Brighton Fringe registration portal shows Ben Carter selected 'No' to operating his own box office. The system confirmed 'No further information is required,' binding Brighton Fringe to this responsibility.

timeline.title: Station Poster Co-Branding Finalised
timeline.event: Ben Carter confirmed final artwork for a Brighton Station co-branded poster campaign promoting Half a Camel and Brighton Fringe. This promotional investment was later erased from institutional narrative.

timeline.title: Box Office Admits System Cannot Track Capacity
timeline.event: Elin Eaton, Fringe Box Office Manager, confirmed that capacity tracking was impossible for unticketed events, directly undermining risk assessments and insurance.

timeline.title: Eventotron Payment Based on Partnership Promise
timeline.event: Ben Carter paid £250 to Eventotron to implement a mirrored ticket system under assurance from Brighton Fringe (Alice Wright) that it would be welcomed and collaborative. This partnership framing was later used to delay brochure delivery and misrepresent intent.

timeline.title: New Venues and Shows Registered While Blocked
timeline.event: Despite Fringe's positioning of collapse, Half a Camel onboarded new acts and venues. Maris & Otter joined, Alec Crane registered, and infrastructure remained live while brochure progress was covertly stalled.

timeline.title: Artist Assumes Ben Carter Is Fringe Due to Months of Silence
timeline.event: An artist confused by a Fringe email about flyering licences contacted them assuming Ben Carter had already handled it. This event highlights the operational void Brighton Fringe had created — Ben was the only point of contact artists had from October 2024 through February 2025.

timeline.title: Co-Branded Poster Misled Public About Safety and Stability
timeline.event: Brighton Fringe and Half a Camel launched a co-branded poster campaign at Brighton Station. The poster featured both logos and gave the public the impression of unified operations and venue safety. In reality, the Fringe knew the venues were uninsurable and the system was failing. The campaign served to drive ticket sales before Ben Carter was erased.
